rows.rationale: KA-C5-001 is a BESCOM guideline but this application is under HESCOM jurisdiction, so the clause does not govern this case. | KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes with 50kWp threshold; the 45kWp system does not require a check meter under current rules. | Clause 4 note ii deems systems up to 150kW feasible, so technical feasibility rejection is unsupported for a 45kWp system.

The proposed system is 45 kWp, which is below the 50 kWp threshold requiring a check meter; thus cl-18 does not mandate rejection. | Clause 4 concerns transformer capacity limits; cumulative 95 kW on 100 kVA transformer is within 80% limit, so it does not block feasibility.

Registry shows GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is superseded as of 2025-07-07; generator should cite GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-check instead. | System is exactly 20 kW, so check meter is optional not mandatory; approval cannot be based on mandatory check meter requirement.
System capacity is exactly 20 kW, so check meter is optional per the clause; since no check meter is provided and it's not required, approval cannot be based on this check meter rule.

Technical feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval cannot be granted as feasibility verification is incomplete. | For LT installations up to 150kW, deemed feasibility applies per KA-C5-006, which was not cited despite being relevant.
The cited clause provides deemed feasibility but does not authorize APPROVAL; the application is still at Technical Feasibility stage with outcome 'Not communicated by the licensee'.
Clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, before application date 2025-09-03.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded before application date 2024-08-04; DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 (effective 2024-04-01) now governs. | Current rule allows GNM capacity up to 5x sanctioned load (max 10MW); 12MW exceeds 10MW cap, but generator cited wrong rule.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-08-08. | Proposed 1.0 kWp does not exceed 100% of 2.0 kW sanctioned load, so rejection is unsupported by applicable regulation.

The clause from GJ-C3-001 was superseded as of the application date (2025-01-03); the amended GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-check should apply. | Check meter is mandatory but absence should not cause rejection; DISCOM installs it at consumer cost per regulation.
The rule requires check meters for systems >20 kW, but absence of check meter at proposal stage is not grounds for rejection since DISCOM installs meters after approval.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising check meter threshold to 50kWp; 80kWp system exceeds this but check meter absence should not cause rejection under old 17.5kW rule.

Registry shows GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is superseded as of 2025-12-02, so cannot be cited as basis for rejection. | Check meters are mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional.
The clause requires check meters only for systems >20 kW; this 12 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not mandatory.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) amended cl-9.2b to allow changes 'twice' per financial year, superseding the 'once' limit cited. | Under amended rules, 2 changes are permitted; applicant made 2 changes with 3-month notice (exceeds 2-month requirement), so application complies.
Clause allows adding connections twice per FY with 2-month notice; applicant made 2 changes but gave 3-month notice, meeting requirements—rejection unsupported.

Clause DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 is marked superseded as of 2025-03-14; the amended DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 applies instead. | The current in-force rule (capacity up to 5x sanctioned load, max 10MW) was not cited or evaluated.

The cited clause applies to ground-mounted GNM capacity limits (max 5x sanctioned load), but the generator failed to verify if the 90 kWp proposal complies with the 600 kW limit (5×120kW) and other applicable GNM eligibility requirements.

TN-C5-001#cl-2 applies only to LT consumers, but applicant's tariff category LB-V Commercial indicates HT/commercial category, not Low Tension. | The later 2021 order governs net feed-in eligibility and should have been considered for the application date.
TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits LT consumers to max 100% of sanctioned demand, but TN-C5-002#cl-I.2 cited by generator applies to HT consumers up to 999kW; LB-V Commercial is LT category.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-009, raising BRPL's SLD waiver cap to 110 MW; the older 75 MW threshold no longer applies. | Generator failed to apply the current 2025 amendment where 50 MW cumulative is within the 110 MW cap, so SLD waiver should still apply.

Clause 3.6 governs SLD/network augmentation cost waivers up to 110 MW for BRPL; cumulative capacity is 50 MW, well under threshold, so this clause does not justify rejection. | The project connects at 33 kV, but the SLD waiver clause applies only to 11 kV and below networks, making the clause irrelevant to rejection. | No rule was cited addressing the actual rejection grounds such as capacity limits, voltage-level eligibility, or GNM registration requirements.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-009, raising TPDDL's SLD waiver cap to 100 MW, so 105 MW cumulative only exceeds the newer threshold. | Clause governs SLD waiver eligibility, not grounds for application rejection at portal registration stage.
Clause sets TPDDL cumulative cap at 100 MW; with project cumulative reaches 105 MW, SLD waiver ends but this doesn't mandate rejection—applicant can pay SLD charges and proceed.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 from 2019-01-04; application date 2023-09-16 requires UP-C3-002#cl-6.2 (75% limit, not 15%). | The applicable 75% DT limit under UP-C3-002#cl-6.2 was not applied; 125 kW is only 78% of 160 kVA, likely approvable.

75% of 160 kVA DT is 120 kW; resultant cumulative capacity 125 kW exceeds this, but existing 110 kW already violates the limit before this application, so rejection reasoning is correct but the threshold math confirms rejection is valid.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded by DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 effective 2024-04-01, before the application date of 2024-06-28. | The amended rule allows GNM capacity up to 5× sanctioned load (max 10MW); 600 kWp is within 5×100kW=500kW limit, so rejection is unsupported.

DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded as of application date 2024-05-22 per registry lookup. | The in-force amended guideline DL-C3-009#cl-3.8 for ground-mounted GNM capacity limits should have been considered.

Clause 3.8 governs Ground Mounted RE Systems, but the application is for a rooftop solar system, not ground-mounted. | Even if applicable, 600 kWp exceeds 5× sanctioned load (5×100kW=500kW), violating the cited capacity limit.

Clause 26 requires SDO to verify feasibility and issue intimation letter, but Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated' so approval is premature. | Systems up to 150kW are deemed feasible per KA-C5-006, which should be cited for automatic feasibility rather than KA-C5-001#cl-26.

The cited clause establishes deemed feasibility, but Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee' and workflow is still at Technical Feasibility stage—approval cannot be granted before DISCOM communicates feasibility.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-006#cl-3.2, extending VNM to all consumers including commercial. | The Seventh Amendment (2025) making VNM applicable to all NCT Delhi consumers was not considered, which would permit this commercial application.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 expands VNM to ALL consumers in NCT Delhi, so NDLT commercial applicant is eligible—this clause supports approval, not rejection. | Proposed 150 kWp exceeds 5× sanctioned load (5×20=100 kW) limit per cl-3(8); generator cited this but did not compute or explain the capacity violation as root cause.

The 50% cap applies to Residential and MSME (Manufacturing) consumers, not HTP-I Industrial consumers like this applicant. | Clause explicitly states no capacity restrictions for captive consumers; this application is for captive consumption, so rejection is unsupported.

HTP-I Industrial tariff category is not a captive consumer or third-party sale; cl-6.2c-ii exemption does not apply. | Non-residential/non-MSME consumers face 50% sanctioned load cap (50 kW), but 80 kWp proposed exceeds this limit.

Registry shows GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 is superseded as of application date 2025-04-24; GJ-C3-003 is the current regulation. | Proposed capacity is 18 kWp (≤20 kW), so check meter is optional, not mandatory; rule does not block or require approval action.

The cited clause makes check meters mandatory only for systems >20 kW; this 18 kWp system is ≤20 kW, so check meter is optional, not a basis for approval. | Clause governs check meter requirements, not application approval decisions; approval criteria rules were not cited.

Clause requires check meter for >17.5kW systems; proposed 30kWp system lacks check meter per EPC proposal, so approval is unsupported. | Newer HESCOM-jurisdiction clause (effective 2025-12-01) raises threshold to 50kWp and may supersede cited clause.

Clause applies only to systems >50kWp; this 30kWp system doesn't trigger check meter requirement, so clause doesn't support approval. | Systems >17.5kW require check meter per KA-C5-001#cl-15; this 30kWp system lacks check meter, violating this rule.

GJ-C3-003 (2020 amendment) supersedes the 65% limit, removing it entirely; the cited 65% threshold is no longer in force. | Under the amended rule (100% limit), 85 kW cumulative ≤ 100 kVA transformer capacity, so rejection is unsupported.
Resultant cumulative solar capacity (85 kW) exceeds the 100 kVA transformer capacity limit, so the clause requires rejection, not approval.

GJ-C3-003 (effective 2020-01-22) amended the 65% limit to 100%, so the original proviso's threshold is superseded. | Under amended rules, 100kVA transformer allows 100kW cumulative; 70kW resultant capacity is within limit, so rejection is incorrect.
Resultant cumulative capacity 70 kW exceeds 100% of 100 kVA transformer capacity (100 kW limit), so application should be rejected, not approved.

KA-C5-006#cl-4-note-ii states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without feasibility reports, making approval premature before DISCOM communicates outcome. | Cited clause requires SDO to verify and issue intimation letter, but Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated', so approval is unsupported.

The deemed feasibility rule eliminates the need for a feasibility report, but does not authorize final APPROVAL when Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee' and workflow is still at Technical Feasibility stage.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 (effective 2025-12-01) supersedes KA-C5-001#cl-15, raising check meter threshold to 50kWp. | Application should cite KA-C5-006#cl-18 requiring check meter only for systems >50kWp; 35kWp system lacks required check meter under old rule but complies under new. | Even if old rule applied, 35kWp >17.5kW requires check meter, but proposal states 'Not provided', so approval is unjustified.

KA-C5-006#cl-18 requires check meters only for systems >50kWp; this 35kWp system falls under KA-C5-001#cl-15 requiring check meters for >17.5kW. | Application's 35kW capacity exceeds 17.5kW threshold requiring a check meter, but 'Solar Check Meter: Not provided' should block approval.

GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 requiring 0.2s accuracy was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22. | Amended regulation requires 1.0 class for Solar Generation Meter; application shows 1.0 class which complies.

Application shows Solar Generation Meter at 1.0 class and Net Meter at 0.5S class, which meets the "1.0 and 0.5S or better" requirement cited. | System is 25 kWp (>20 kW), requiring mandatory Check Meter per cl-13.5-check, but application shows "Solar Check Meter: Not provided" - this violation was not cited as rejection reason.
Proposed 10 kWp exceeds 100% of 8 kW sanctioned load, but Net Billing mode is requested, not Net Feed-in; TN-C5-002 allows Net Billing for all consumers without the 100% cap restriction.

Cited clause permits capacity up to sanctioned load (8 kW) up to 999 kW max; 10 kWp exceeds 8 kW sanctioned load, but rejection reason misquotes clause as disqualifying rather than noting capacity exceeds sanctioned load limit.

DL-C3-006#cl-3.2 from 2020 is superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 (effective 2026-01-20) which expanded VNM to all consumers. | Applicant is NDLT Non-Domestic with commercial shops, not domestic/charitable category covered under the cited 2020 clause. | The current 2025 amendment extending VNM to all NCT Delhi consumers should have been cited instead.

VNM clause applies to consumer eligibility, but application proposes 120 kWp system against 30 kW sanctioned load, violating typical capacity limits not addressed. | No rule cited for maximum allowable solar capacity relative to sanctioned load; Delhi regulations typically cap rooftop solar at sanctioned load.

GJ-C3-003 (2020 amendment) supersedes the 65% limit, removing it entirely to allow cumulative capacity up to 100% of transformer capacity. | The amended 2020 regulation allowing 100% transformer capacity was not cited despite being the applicable in-force rule.
Resultant cumulative capacity (55 kW) exceeds transformer capacity (100 kVA), violating the 100% limit; application should be REJECTED, not APPROVED.

UP-C3-001 was superseded by UP-C3-002 effective 2019-01-04, before the application date of 2023-04-19. | Under the applicable 2019 regulation, 5 kWp does not exceed 100% of 4 kW connected demand; the rejection is arithmetically incorrect.

Proposed 5 kWp exceeds 100% of 4 kW sanctioned load, but connected load equals sanctioned load, so the generator incorrectly cited this clause without computing the actual violation threshold correctly or considering that 5 kWp > 4 kW is the real basis.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.6 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-009#cl-3.6, raising BRPL's SLD waiver cap to 110 MW. | Cumulative capacity is 95 MW, which is below the amended 110 MW cap for BRPL, so SLD waiver applies and approval may be correct, but wrong clause was cited. | Under the cited (outdated) clause, 95 MW exceeds BRPL's 75 MW cap, which would block approval, contradicting the decision.

The cited clause sets BRPL's cumulative GNM/VNM capacity limit at 110 MW; with this project, cumulative capacity reaches 95 MW which is within limit, but the clause only waives SLD charges—it does not authorize approval of a 400 kWp system exceeding 100 kW sanctioned load. | The cited clause addresses SLD waiver, not the core eligibility criteria for system capacity limits relative to sanctioned load for GNM applications.

GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 applies to Residential Consumers and MSME (Manufacturing) Enterprises, but applicant is HTP-I Industrial tariff category. | Clause applies to captive consumers without capacity restrictions, but application is for net metering, not captive use without net metering. | Net metering capacity limit of 1kW-1000kW should be verified but was not cited by generator.

HTP-I Industrial tariff does not qualify as 'captive consumer' or 'Third Party Sale'; the clause removes capacity restrictions only for those specific categories, not general industrial consumers. | For non-residential, non-MSME consumers, capacity is limited to 50% of sanctioned load (150 kW), but proposed 120 kWp complies; however, this rule was not cited by generator.

TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits net feed-in capacity to 100% of sanctioned demand (4 kW), but the application requests Net Billing mode, not net feed-in, so this clause does not justify rejection. | TN-C5-002 allows net billing for all consumer categories without the 100% sanctioned load cap applicable to net metering/net feed-in, which was not considered.

The cited clause permits systems up to 999 kW for net billing; the 6 kWp proposal exceeds the 4 kW sanctioned load limit per TN-C5-001#cl-2, not TN-C5-002#cl-I.2. | TN-C5-001#cl-2 limits rooftop solar to 100% of sanctioned demand (4 kW), which the 6 kWp system violates; this rule should have been cited.

UP-C3-001 was superseded on 2019-01-04; application dated 2023-07-04 should use UP-C3-002#cl-6.2 with 75% threshold. | Under current UP-C3-002#cl-6.2, 75% of 100 kVA = 75 kW; 78 kW cumulative exceeds limit, but correct rule was not cited.
Resultant 78 kW on 100 kVA DT equals 78%, exceeding 75% limit; however existing 72 kW already exceeds 75% (72%), so rejection is correct but root cause misattributes fault to this application.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) amended cl-9.2b to allow changes 'twice' per year, superseding the 'once' limit cited. | The amended rule permitting two changes per year was not applied; applicant's single prior change does not exhaust the limit.
Clause allows twice per FY with 2-month notice; applicant made 1 prior change (below limit of 2) but gave only 1-month notice instead of required 2 months—rejection reason cites wrong ground.

Application was submitted 2023-12-05 (before Feb 2024), qualifying under Phase II, but CFA claim deadline was extended to 31.12.2025 per IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended, making Oct 2024 cutoff inapplicable. | Amended rule extends CFA claim deadline to 31.12.2025 for Phase II applications; claim received 2026-02-16 still exceeds this, but wrong cutoff was cited.

Phase II applications have CFA deadline of 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-02-16 is after deadline, but generator garbled the rule text and cited October 2024 deadline which applies to Phase I only. | Generator failed to cite IN-C1-011 which confirms Phase II applications submitted before 13 Feb 2024 remain eligible for CFA under revised subsidy rates.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-009 with updated TPDDL cumulative capacity limit of 100 MW. | Current cumulative capacity (120 MW) exceeds TPDDL's 100 MW threshold under DL-C3-015, so SLD waiver does not apply. | Application shows SLD charges were paid, contradicting approval rationale citing SLD waiver eligibility.
Cumulative TPDDL capacity is 120 MW, exceeding the 100 MW threshold in cl-3.6, so SLD waiver should not apply and approval is unsupported.

Clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5 was superseded by GJ-C3-003 amendment effective 2020-01-22, before application date 2025-05-15. | Superseding regulation requires Solar Meter accuracy 1.0 class, but proposal shows 0.5S which may not meet current requirements for solar generation meter.

Regulation requires Solar Meter accuracy of 1.0 class, but EPC proposal shows Solar Generation Meter at 0.5S class; while 0.5S exceeds requirement, the cited rule alone doesn't justify full approval of the application. | For 15 kWp system (≤20 kW), check meter rules apply but were not evaluated in the decision.

KA-C5-006 states installations up to 150kW are deemed feasible without feasibility reports, superseding the SDO verification process cited. | Technical Feasibility Outcome is 'Not communicated by the licensee', so approval cannot be granted yet.

The deemed feasibility rule applies only to LT installations per Note-i, but the application is for LT-3 Commercial tariff which may require explicit feasibility verification under KA-C5-001#cl-26. | SDO must verify technical feasibility and issue intimation letter; feasibility outcome is 'Not communicated' so approval is premature.

The amended clause IN-C1-001#cl-annex1-ii-amended extends the CFA deadline for Phase II applications at inspected/installed stage to 31.12.2025, which was not considered. | Application was installed and inspected before 01.04.2025, so the extended deadline of 31.12.2025 under the amended clause applies, not the October 2024 cutoff.

Phase II applications are admissible for CFA if claim received till 31.12.2025; CFA claim received 2026-01-15 is after deadline, but generator misquoted October 2024 deadline which applies only to Phase I.

DL-C3-015 (effective 2026-01-20) supersedes DL-C3-006#cl-3.2, extending VNM eligibility to all consumers in NCT Delhi. | The 2025 Seventh Amendment making VNM applicable to all Delhi consumers was not considered, which would allow this domestic application.

DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 explicitly allows VNM for all Delhi consumers, so it supports approval, not rejection. | 200 kWp exceeds 5× sanctioned load (150 kW max), but this is a capacity limit violation, not a metering mode eligibility issue.
